summary: Runner study: 101 closed paper trades, average -4.5% (median -20.1%, 15% won, -6.5% without the single best trade).
Risk rules: Listed (-2.8%) and dropped (-7.6%) coins did about the same so far.

Numbers that reliably separated winners from losers (luck-corrected): 24h change over 100% (+395013.3% against +146.4%); Hour of day (UTC) 12-18 (+353115.5% against +151.7%); 24h change under 25% (-14.6% against +188239.6%).
Against random coins: The runners list (-2.8%) and random coins (+115542.4%) did about the same so far.
Locked test (from 2026-10-25): 4 of 4 rules found before the lock date also held on 15 later trades.
Week by week: 24h change over 100% pointed the same way in 2 of 2 weeks; Hour of day (UTC) 12-18 pointed the same way in 2 of 2 weeks.

Risk: at 10% of the account per trade the listed runners had a worst drawdown of 34.4% and a longest losing run of 22. A size of about 6.6% per trade would keep 24 losses in a row under a 30% account hit.
Progress: 101 of 30 closed trades needed before reading results (0 to go).
notes: Returns are paper returns after 3% entry slippage plus the price impact of a $1,000 order on the pool liquidity. They ignore gas, exit liquidity and rugs, so real results would be lower. One huge winner can lift an average, so the median and the average without the best trade are shown.
